sentences.en: Hello everyone, it's Tom here with news of a Rest Is History special.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是汤姆，为大家带来一期《历史的休息》特别节目。

sentences.en: I am interviewing none other than the great, the one and only Paul McCartney.
sentences.zh: 我采访的嘉宾不是别人，正是那位伟大、独一无二的保罗·麦卡特尼。

sentences.en: He has a new album out, The Boys of Dungeon Lane.
sentences.zh: 他有一张新专辑即将发布，名为《地牢巷的男孩们》。

sentences.en: Lots of the songs on that album are about his early years growing up in Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 专辑里的许多歌曲都讲述了他早年在利物浦成长的岁月。

sentences.en: So I'm talking to him about that, about the context, the history that gave rise to the Beatles.
sentences.zh: 所以我正与他聊这些，聊聊背景，聊聊孕育了披头士乐队的那段历史。

sentences.en: And we have a world exclusive here because one of the songs from that album, Salesman's Saint, will be featuring in the interview.
sentences.zh: 我们这里有一个全球独家首发，因为专辑中的一首歌《推销员的圣徒》将在采访中首次亮相。

sentences.en: So incredibly exciting.
sentences.zh: 真是令人无比兴奋。

sentences.en: Enjoy the song.
sentences.zh: 请欣赏这首歌。

sentences.en: Enjoy the interview.
sentences.zh: 请欣赏这段采访。

sentences.en: This episode is brought to you by Lloyd's, which has been backing British ambition for over 250 years.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由劳埃德银行赞助播出，该行已支持英国雄心壮志超过250年。

sentences.en: Now, when you think about it, every dynasty in history has boiled down to two important elements, aspiration and action.
sentences.zh: 现在，仔细想想，历史上每一个王朝的兴衰都归结为两个重要因素：抱负与行动。

sentences.en: And a classic example of this from British history, the rise of the House of Wessex,
sentences.zh: 英国历史上一个经典的例子就是威塞克斯王朝的崛起，

sentences.en: the family of Alfred the Great and his heirs, who between them established the United Kingdom of England.
sentences.zh: 也就是阿尔弗雷德大帝及其继承人的家族，他们共同建立了英格兰联合王国。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a great story, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 没错，这是一个很棒的故事，不是吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: A great lesson in leadership, I think, for anybody.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对任何人来说都是一堂很好的领导力课程。

sentences.en: So Alfred and his heirs, they marry idealism and pragmatism.
sentences.zh: 所以阿尔弗雷德和他的继承人们，他们将理想主义与实用主义结合在了一起。

sentences.en: They're brilliant at alliances.
sentences.zh: 他们非常擅长结盟。

sentences.en: They're brilliant at managing power.
sentences.zh: 他们非常擅长驾驭权力。

sentences.en: They're brilliant, of course, at managing their money, which is a key part of political leadership.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们也非常擅长理财，这是政治领导力的关键部分。

sentences.en: And of course, we are all reaping the rewards of their wisdom and foresight.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们现在都在享受他们智慧和远见带来的成果。

sentences.en: When it's time to make your next move, you can bank on Lloyd's to be ready when you are.
sentences.zh: 当您准备好迈出下一步时，您可以信赖劳埃德银行，我们随时为您准备就绪。

sentences.en: Because from new businesses to new homes and new life chapters, backed by generations of hope and ambition,
sentences.zh: 因为从新企业到新家园，再到人生的新篇章，在几代人的希望与抱负支持下，

sentences.en: you can see, Tom, why 14 million people trust Lloyd's to help make their dreams a reality.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你可以看出为什么1400万人信任劳埃德银行，帮助他们实现梦想。

sentences.en: Based on Lloyd's internal customer data from March 2026.
sentences.zh: 基于劳埃德银行2026年3月的内部客户数据。

sentences.en: Hello, everyone, and welcome to The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听《历史的休息》。

sentences.en: And obviously, on this show, we have talked about all kinds of world historical figures.
sentences.zh: 显然，在这个节目中，我们讨论过各种各样的世界历史人物。

sentences.en: But today is a first because it's the first time on the show that I will actually be talking to a world historical figure.
sentences.zh: 但今天是一个先例，因为这是节目中第一次真正与一位世界历史人物对话。

sentences.en: And this is a man who is the greatest composer of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 他是一位被公认为20世纪最伟大的作曲家。

sentences.en: With the Beatles, he was a lightning rod for one of the most transformative decades in modern history.
sentences.zh: 作为披头士乐队的一员，他是现代史上最具变革性的十年中的核心人物。

sentences.en: And ever since I was about eight, he has been my personal hero.
sentences.zh: 从我大约八岁起，他就是我个人的英雄。

sentences.en: So this is unbelievably exciting for me.
sentences.zh: 所以这对我来说简直太令人兴奋了。

sentences.en: And I am talking about, of course, Paul McCartney.
sentences.zh: 我所说的当然就是保罗·麦卡特尼。

sentences.en: Well, that's quite an intro.
sentences.zh: 哇，这开场白真是太隆重了。

sentences.en: It's not too much for you, I hope.
sentences.zh: 希望没有让你感到压力太大。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Not exactly.
sentences.zh: 没那么夸张。

sentences.en: Hey, come on.
sentences.zh: 嘿，别这样。

sentences.en: Adulation, I don't mind at all.
sentences.zh: 这种赞美，我一点也不介意。

sentences.en: So we're talking because you've got a new album out.
sentences.zh: 我们今天聊天是因为你有一张新专辑要发布了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is an album that, it's not continuously about it, but a lot of the songs are focused on your childhood, your teenage years, growing up in Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 这张专辑虽然不是通篇都在讲，但很多歌都聚焦于你的童年、少年时期，以及在利物浦的成长经历。

sentences.en: And I was wondering, is this telling us something about what made Paul McCartney who he is?
sentences.zh: 我在想，这是否揭示了是什么造就了今天的保罗·麦卡特尼？

sentences.en: In other words, could Paul McCartney, could the Beatles have emerged from any other city apart from Liverpool, do you think?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你认为保罗·麦卡特尼，或者说披头士乐队，有可能诞生在利物浦以外的任何其他城市吗？

sentences.en: Was there something distinctive about Liverpool?
sentences.zh: 利物浦有什么独特之处吗？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was thinking about it recently.
sentences.zh: 是的，我最近也在思考这个问题。

sentences.en: I do think the character of Liverpool is a very strong one.
sentences.zh: 我确实认为利物浦的性格非常鲜明。

sentences.en: I think with the Irish influence, and then coming through the war, and having to be happy when bombs were falling.
sentences.zh: 我认为这与爱尔兰的影响有关，还有经历过战争，在炸弹落下时依然要保持快乐。

sentences.en: So there was a lot of music when I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 所以我小时候听过很多音乐。

sentences.en: My dad played the piano at home.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸在家里弹钢琴。

sentences.en: There were a lot of jokes.
sentences.zh: 有很多笑话。

sentences.en: And so they kept their heads, you know, above water by laughing at the whole thing.
sentences.zh: 他们通过嘲笑这一切来让自己保持乐观，你知道的。

sentences.en: And I think that was something that found its way into the Beatles.
sentences.zh: 我认为这种精神也融入到了披头士乐队中。

sentences.en: And I think it gave us a good sense of humor that no matter what we were going to do, like arrive in America and have the New York press ready to make fun of us,
sentences.zh: 它给了我们很好的幽默感，无论我们要去做什么，比如抵达美国时面对准备嘲笑我们的纽约媒体，

sentences.en: because we gave as good as we got, and that was because of our Liverpool upbringing.
sentences.zh: 我们都能从容应对，这都要归功于我们在利物浦的成长经历。

sentences.en: So you, in the new album, you have this song, Salesman, Saint, which is about your parents, your mum and dad.
sentences.zh: 所以，在新专辑里，你有一首歌叫《推销员的圣徒》，是关于你父母的。

sentences.en: And it kind of begins actually in the war, because you were born in 1942.
sentences.zh: 它其实是从战争时期开始的，因为你出生于1942年。

sentences.en: All the Beatles were born in the war.
sentences.zh: 所有的披头士成员都出生在战争期间。

sentences.en: How much of a kind of legacy did the war years leave in Liverpool and on your kind of personal memories of it?
sentences.zh: 战争岁月在利物浦以及你个人的记忆中留下了多深的烙印？

sentences.en: A lot.
sentences.zh: 很深。

sentences.en: You were very aware of it.
sentences.zh: 你对此非常有感知。

sentences.en: Not the actual bombing.
sentences.zh: 不是指实际的轰炸。

sentences.en: I think all of us were a little too young to experience much of that.
sentences.zh: 我想我们所有人都太小了，没经历过太多那种场面。

sentences.en: Ringo, who's the oldest, he might have some memories, but I don't.
sentences.zh: 林戈是年纪最大的，他可能有一些记忆，但我没有。

sentences.en: But the thing is, you know, the feeling that the grown-ups had, as I say, you know, having to laugh it off.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，你知道，大人们的那种感觉，就像我说的，必须一笑置之。

sentences.en: This is a world war.
sentences.zh: 这是一场世界大战。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But they're just, they've got to carry on, they've got to talk to each other.
sentences.zh: 但他们必须继续生活，必须互相交谈。

sentences.en: Because that's one of the lines in the song, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 因为那是歌词里的一句，不是吗？

sentences.en: They had to carry on.
sentences.zh: 他们必须坚持下去。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they did.
sentences.zh: 他们做到了。

sentences.en: That's what I say, you know.
sentences.zh: 这就是我想说的，你知道。

sentences.en: And I marvel at that, because now, you know, I mean, people can get defeated by the slightest little thing.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到惊叹，因为现在，人们可能会被一点点小事打败。

sentences.en: So compare that to not being defeated by bombs literally raining down on your city.
sentences.zh: 所以对比一下，那些在炸弹真正倾泻在城市上空时都没有被打败的人。

sentences.en: And you've got to find a way around it.
sentences.zh: 你必须找到应对的方法。

sentences.en: And so when I grew up, there was a lot of joy.
sentences.zh: 所以当我长大时，生活中有很多快乐。

sentences.en: I think everyone was just so glad to be out of these terrible circumstances.
sentences.zh: 我想每个人都只是很高兴能从那些可怕的环境中走出来。

sentences.en: And my uncles were all great joke tellers.
sentences.zh: 我的叔叔们都很会讲笑话。

sentences.en: And I never heard any of them sort of sitting around going, oh, God, life's terrible.
sentences.zh: 我从没听过他们坐在那儿说，哦，天哪，生活太糟糕了。

sentences.en: You know, there was none of that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，完全没有那种事。

sentences.en: It just, they'd come through it.
sentences.zh: 他们只是挺过来了。

sentences.en: And so it kind of wasn't allowed.
sentences.zh: 所以那种消极情绪是不被允许的。

sentences.en: So the bomb damage in Liverpool, it took a long time to repair, right?
sentences.zh: 所以利物浦的炸弹损毁，花了很长时间才修复，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then you went to Hamburg.
sentences.zh: 然后你去了汉堡。

sentences.en: And Hamburg also was a city that had been wiped out.
sentences.zh: 汉堡也是一座被夷为平地的城市。

sentences.en: So when you were kind of making your music, were you aware, were you thinking of, oh, thank God, you know, we're not involved in that.
sentences.zh: 所以当你创作音乐时，你是否意识到，或者在想，哦，谢天谢地，我们没有卷入其中。

sentences.en: You voided national service by, I think, by about a year, didn't you?
sentences.zh: 你避开了国民兵役，我想大概晚了一年，对吧？

sentences.en: A year or two.
sentences.zh: 一两年吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Was the fact that the war had passed and you were kind of in a new age and Liverpool was starting to get back on its feet, was that something that kind of served as an inspiration?
sentences.zh: 战争已经结束，你处于一个新时代，利物浦开始恢复元气，这是否成为了一种灵感来源？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: You know, as I say, all of us grew up expecting to go in the army or national service.
sentences.zh: 你知道，正如我所说，我们所有人在成长过程中都以为自己要参军或服国民兵役。

sentences.en: So we were all kind of coasting through our teenage years thinking, oh, my God, it's going to happen soon.
sentences.zh: 所以我们在青少年时期都过得战战兢兢，心想，天哪，这事儿很快就要发生了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then suddenly it was as if God opened the waters and the Israelites could just go through.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间，就像上帝劈开了水面，以色列人得以通过一样。

sentences.en: And that was us.
sentences.zh: 那就是我们。

sentences.en: We suddenly, all of that had gone, except for the evidence of it.
sentences.zh: 我们突然间，这一切都过去了，只剩下战争留下的痕迹。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So where we played football would be on what we called the Bomby, which was the bombsite.
sentences.zh: 所以我们踢足球的地方就是我们所谓的“炸弹坑”，也就是被炸毁的遗址。

sentences.en: And we didn't think anything of it, it was just the Bomby.
sentences.zh: 我们对此习以为常，那只是“炸弹坑”而已。

sentences.en: But later then you go, why did we call it the Bomby?
sentences.zh: 但后来你会想，为什么我们叫它炸弹坑？

sentences.en: Also, if there's an unexploded bomb.
sentences.zh: 而且，如果那里还有未爆炸的炸弹。

sentences.en: It could.
sentences.zh: 确实可能。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, you know, so that was all around us, but we just lived with it and kind of made it part of our lives.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，这一切都在我们周围，我们只是与它共存，并把它变成了我们生活的一部分。

sentences.en: And then we were able to, like our parents, able to kind of laugh at everything.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就能像我们的父母一样，能够对一切一笑置之。

sentences.en: And today is, we're recording this on International Midwife Day, apparently.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们录制节目的日子正好是国际助产士日。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇。

sentences.en: And so that song, Salesman and Saint, your dad was a salesman.
sentences.zh: 所以那首歌《推销员与圣徒》，你父亲是个推销员。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And your mom was obviously a saint, but she was more specifically a midwife.
sentences.zh: 而你母亲显然是一位圣徒，但更具体地说，她是一位助产士。

sentences.en: My father was a salesman, my mother was a saint, working every God-given minute, and making love to pay the rent.
sentences.zh: 我父亲是推销员，我母亲是圣徒，她每时每刻都在辛勤工作，为了支付房租而奔波。

sentences.en: The war was nearly over, the peace would soon begin, living on the edge of the city.
sentences.zh: 战争即将结束，和平即将开始，生活在城市边缘。

sentences.en: That was very important, wasn't it, in terms of where you would live?
sentences.zh: 这很重要，不是吗，关于你住在哪里？

sentences.en: Because as a midwife, she would get kind of houses, and you would kind of move around upgrading with each house.
sentences.zh: 因为作为助产士，她会得到一些房子，你们会随着每次搬家而改善居住条件。

sentences.en: It's true, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是真的，没错。

sentences.en: We moved around quite a lot and didn't realize until we were much older that, ah, that's why we moved.
sentences.zh: 我们搬了很多次家，直到长大后才意识到，啊，原来这就是我们搬家的原因。

sentences.en: But, yeah, she would, and it was often on the edge of the city, you know.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，她会，而且通常是在城市边缘，你知道。

sentences.en: But there were nice houses, you know.
sentences.zh: 但那都是不错的房子，你知道。

sentences.en: It was always an upgrade to us.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说总是升级。

sentences.en: Because Hawthorne Road had an indoor toilet, didn't it, I think?
sentences.zh: 因为霍桑路那栋房子有室内厕所，对吧，我想？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: An indoor toilet.
sentences.zh: 室内厕所。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, it's true.
sentences.zh: 是的，不，是真的。

sentences.en: So, you know, we thought we were going somewhere.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们觉得我们有出息了。

sentences.en: And my mom was very aspirational, like a lot of good mothers.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈很有抱负，像许多好母亲一样。

sentences.en: She just wanted her kids to succeed, do well.
sentences.zh: 她只是希望她的孩子们成功，过得好。

sentences.en: I mean, my wife, Nancy, she will say to me, you don't talk Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 我的妻子南希常对我说，你说话没有利物浦口音。

sentences.en: She said, people love it when you talk Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 她说，人们喜欢听你讲利物浦话。

sentences.en: I said, yeah, but my mom tried to get us not to talk Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 我说，是啊，但我妈以前总是试图让我们不要讲利物浦话。

sentences.en: She tried to get us to talk posh.
sentences.zh: 她试图让我们讲那种时髦的口音。

sentences.en: She thought, she was hoping we'd be doctors or something, you know.
sentences.zh: 她当时希望我们能成为医生什么的，你知道。

sentences.en: But I guess as a midwife, she's a community midwife, right?
sentences.zh: 但我猜作为助产士，她是社区助产士，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, she's not working in a hospital.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，她不是在医院工作。

sentences.en: So she has to serve all the community.
sentences.zh: 所以她必须为整个社区服务。

sentences.en: So there would be, I don't know, people in leafy homes, and then there would be people
sentences.zh: 所以会有，我不知道，住在绿树成荫的房子里的人，也会有生活贫困的人，

sentences.en: with very little, and she would have to serve them all, and presumably she would know them all.
sentences.zh: 她必须为所有人服务，想必她认识他们所有人。

sentences.en: Yeah, no, it's quite, it's something growing up.
sentences.zh: 是的，不，这确实是成长过程中的一部分。

sentences.en: Oh, my mom's a midwife.
sentences.zh: 哦，我妈妈是助产士。

sentences.en: And you don't really think much beyond that.
sentences.zh: 你当时并不会想太多。

sentences.en: But now you think, wow, you know, just going out and home delivering all these babies and the parents being so in love with you, I mean, they would come around to our house
sentences.zh: 但现在你会想，哇，你知道，只是出去为所有这些婴儿接生，父母们是多么爱戴她，我的意思是，他们会来到我们家，

sentences.en: and bringing little gifts, a little statuette or something, very cheap stuff.
sentences.zh: 带些小礼物，一个小雕像什么的，非常便宜的东西。

sentences.en: But just to show the gratitude.
sentences.zh: 但只是为了表达感激之情。

sentences.en: I have one big memory of her.
sentences.zh: 我有一个关于她的大记忆。

sentences.en: It was in the winter, and it had been a heavy snowfall, and she got called up, because we had a phone, one phone in the house, and she got called to go to a berth.
sentences.zh: 那是在冬天，下了一场大雪，她接到电话，因为我们家有一部电话，家里唯一的电话，她被叫去接生。

sentences.en: So she got on her bike, because they didn't have cars.
sentences.zh: 于是她骑上了自行车，因为他们没有车。

sentences.en: She got on her bike in this deep snow with her uniform on, with her little suitcase on the back and her little basket on the front.
sentences.zh: 她穿着制服，背着小手提箱，车前挂着小篮子，骑进了深雪里。

sentences.en: And I have this memory in the streetlights of us cycling out through the snow and thinking, wow, that's pretty brave.
sentences.zh: 我记忆中在路灯下，看着她骑车穿过雪地，心想，哇，那真是太勇敢了。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, you did it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，你做到了。

sentences.en: They did it.
sentences.zh: 他们做到了。

sentences.en: I was asked to ask you this by my wife, who's a midwife, so she will be delighted by absolutely everything that you've said there.
sentences.zh: 我妻子让我问你这个问题，她是位助产士，所以她一定会对你刚才说的每一句话都感到高兴。

sentences.en: So just sticking with your parents, two other things specific about Liverpool, maybe what makes it distinctive, related to your parents.
sentences.zh: 那么，继续聊聊你的父母，关于利物浦还有两件特别的事，也许是让它与众不同的地方，和你父母有关。

sentences.en: So both of them kind of came from Ireland, ultimately.
sentences.zh: 他们俩最终都是从爱尔兰来的。

sentences.en: I think their origins are in Ireland.
sentences.zh: 我想他们的根在爱尔兰。

sentences.en: Their family came from Ireland, yeah.
sentences.zh: 他们的家族来自爱尔兰，没错。

sentences.en: So that kind of generates a sense in Liverpool that it's not quite part of England, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这在利物浦产生了一种感觉，觉得它不完全属于英格兰，不是吗？

sentences.en: Do you think that was a kind of important part of...
sentences.zh: 你认为那是……重要的一部分吗？

sentences.en: I'd never thought of it like that, but you're right, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我从来没那样想过，但你说得对，确实如此。

sentences.en: No, we were from Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 不，我们是利物浦人。

sentences.en: And, you know, you didn't want to be lumped in with everyone.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你不想被和所有人混为一谈。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: We were like, we thought we were special.
sentences.zh: 我们当时觉得，我们很特别。

sentences.en: And I think at one point it was the second city to London because it was a big port.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得在某个时期，它是仅次于伦敦的第二大城市，因为它是一个大港口。

sentences.en: Yeah, fabulously rich.
sentences.zh: 没错，极其富有。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So, you know, we had a great sense of importance, which waned through the years, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们有一种强烈的优越感，虽然这些年来逐渐减弱了。

sentences.en: But when I was growing up, you definitely thought Liverpool was a very great, grand historic place.
sentences.zh: 但我成长的时候，你绝对会认为利物浦是一个非常伟大、宏伟的历史名城。

sentences.en: You used to go down and see all the liners off.
sentences.zh: 你以前常去码头送别所有的远洋客轮。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: They'd all be going off to Canada, you know, places like that.
sentences.zh: 它们都会开往加拿大，你知道，诸如此类的地方。

sentences.en: And it was only later that you learn that this was slave trade.
sentences.zh: 后来你才知道，那是奴隶贸易。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: That there was a lot of that.
sentences.zh: 那样的交易有很多。

sentences.en: Only thing we would see would be the local Caribbean people.
sentences.zh: 我们唯一能见到的就是当地的加勒比人。

sentences.en: So we would know people that would be descended.
sentences.zh: 所以我们认识一些他们的后代。

sentences.en: We didn't talk about it then.
sentences.zh: 那时我们并不谈论这个。

sentences.en: But there was, I guess, a sense of Liverpool as being open to the world as well as to the rest of England.
sentences.zh: 但我猜，利物浦确实有一种面向世界，同时也面向英格兰其他地区的感觉。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So that what is often said about Liverpool is that it's more open to, say, musical influences perhaps than other places.
sentences.zh: 所以关于利物浦常说的一点是，它比其他地方更容易受到音乐等各方面的影响。

sentences.en: Do you think that that was true?
sentences.zh: 你觉得那是真的吗？

sentences.en: Because, of course, you know, your love of rock and roll was fundamental to what became the Beatles.
sentences.zh: 因为当然了，你知道，你对摇滚乐的热爱是披头士乐队成立的基础。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And, you know, sailors came back from a particularly merchant navy.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，水手们回来了，特别是商船队的水手。

sentences.en: A lot of them that we would know came back from America, whether they'd been to, like, New Orleans or, you know, down south.
sentences.zh: 我们认识的很多人都是从美国回来的，不管他们是去过新奥尔良，还是去过南方。

sentences.en: And they had records that nobody else had.
sentences.zh: 他们手里有别人没有的唱片。

sentences.en: So how would you get hold of them?
sentences.zh: 那你怎么弄到这些唱片呢？

sentences.en: You'd just, you know, you'd borrow them off somebody.
sentences.zh: 你就是，你知道，你找人借。

sentences.en: Somebody would know the sailor who had it and the sailor would let them borrow it.
sentences.zh: 有人会认识那个有唱片的水手，然后水手会让他们借走。

sentences.en: You'd borrow it off them.
sentences.zh: 你从他们那儿借来。

sentences.en: So it was like a little culture where you'd, the record would go around and we'd all learn it.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像一个小圈子，唱片会传阅，我们大家都会学着唱。

sentences.en: Because I think for people of subsequent generations, it's hard to get our heads around how difficult it was to access music.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得对于后几代人来说，很难理解当时获取音乐有多么困难。

sentences.en: You know, we can get it on whatever, just stream it or whatever now.
sentences.zh: 你知道，现在我们随便怎么弄，流媒体播放就行了。

sentences.en: But the idea that it's actually really quite hard to get the physical records or to find the radio stations that it's being played on.
sentences.zh: 但当时想要买到实体唱片，或者找到播放这些音乐的电台，其实真的非常困难。

sentences.en: And so does that make, did that make it, if you were interested in rock and roll or whatever, that you were the,
sentences.zh: 那么这是否意味着，如果你对摇滚乐感兴趣，你就是……

sentences.en: you were kind of a self-selecting group of people who would know what you were talking about when you met up and discussed these people?
sentences.zh: 你属于那种自选的小群体，见面讨论这些歌手时，大家都心知肚明？

sentences.en: Yeah, that was, that was what it was.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是那样。

sentences.en: That was, um, you would know certain chords and then someone would know an extra chord.
sentences.zh: 就是，嗯，你会弹某些和弦，然后有人会弹一个额外的和弦。

sentences.en: So you would go to his house and learn this extra chord and you build up your knowledge through things like that.
sentences.zh: 于是你会去他家学这个额外的和弦，通过这种方式积累你的知识。

sentences.en: There was, none of us ever learned to read or write music, which is kind of an interesting fact about all the, pretty much all the groups out of the sixties.
sentences.zh: 我们中没有人学过识谱或写谱，这对于六十年代几乎所有的乐队来说都是一个有趣的事实。

sentences.en: Do I remember talking to Jeff Lynne of ELO?
sentences.zh: 我记得我和ELO乐队的杰夫·琳恩聊过吗？

sentences.en: He says, oh, we just made it up and that's what it was.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，我们就是自己编出来的，就是这样。

sentences.en: We made it up, but there's a great strength in me showing you a chord or a riff or something.
sentences.zh: 我们是编出来的，但这种我教你一个和弦或一段即兴重复段的感觉非常有力量。

sentences.en: And it's just going from mind to mind.
sentences.zh: 它就在脑海之间传递。

sentences.en: There's no paper involved.
sentences.zh: 不需要纸张。

sentences.en: All of what we did, I mean, you know, in this very studio would be that.
sentences.zh: 我们所做的一切，我的意思是，你知道，就在这个录音室里，都是这样。

sentences.en: It was really immediate transference of ideas.
sentences.zh: 这真的是思想的即时传递。

sentences.en: And, you know, I, I say, if you look back on all, all our histories and our legacy, it was kind of bardic.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我说，如果你回顾我们所有的历史和遗产，它有点像吟游诗人式的。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of them didn't write it down.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们很多人并没有写下来。

sentences.en: You know, Irish music was not really, I don't think, written down.
sentences.zh: 你知道，爱尔兰音乐真的没有被写下来，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: It was just played and you learned it and then you played it your way.
sentences.zh: 它就是被演奏出来，你学会了，然后用你的方式去演奏。

sentences.en: So we had a lot of that.
sentences.zh: 所以我们有很多这样的经历。

sentences.en: And that, that was really nice.
sentences.zh: 那真的很棒。

sentences.en: Um, for transference of ideas, you would just, should just, we would come in here on a Monday morning, let's say, if we were going to record during the week.
sentences.zh: 嗯，为了传递思想，你只需要……我们会在周一早上来到这里，假设我们这周要录音的话。

sentences.en: And it would mainly, in the beginning, be John and I, and we would have just written something the week before, written some songs.
sentences.zh: 起初主要是约翰和我，我们前一周刚写了一些东西，写了一些歌。

sentences.en: And we'd come in and everyone would just gather 10 o'clock, 10.30 in the morning.
sentences.zh: 我们进来，大家在早上10点、10点半聚齐。

sentences.en: And George Martin would say, okay, well, what is it, what are you going to do?
sentences.zh: 乔治·马丁会说，好吧，是什么，你们打算做什么？

sentences.en: And we'd say, oh, well, there's this one.
sentences.zh: 我们会说，哦，有这一首。

sentences.en: And we'd, we'd play it.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就会演奏它。

sentences.en: Me and John, on two acoustics, we'd play it.
sentences.zh: 我和约翰，用两把木吉他演奏它。

sentences.en: And George Harrison would look at it and go, okay.
sentences.zh: 乔治·哈里森会看一眼然后说，好的。

sentences.en: Because immediately he knew what we knew.
sentences.zh: 因为他立刻就知道我们所知道的。

sentences.en: We'd all learned it all together.
sentences.zh: 我们大家一起学会了它。

sentences.en: Ringo would tap out a rhythm kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 林戈会敲出一种节奏之类的东西。

sentences.en: And we trusted him to know what to do.
sentences.zh: 我们信任他，知道他该怎么做。

sentences.en: And then 20 minutes later, we were recording that song that no one had ever heard, including the producer.
sentences.zh: 然后20分钟后，我们就在录制那首没人听过的歌了，包括制作人在内。

sentences.en: Well, I think, I mean, I think for anyone who's seen the, um, the Get Back film, watching you come up with Get Back,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想，我的意思是，对于任何看过《Get Back》电影的人来说，看着你们创作《Get Back》的过程，

sentences.en: it's been revelatory in those terMs. You're kind of, come on, it's Get Back.
sentences.zh: 那在这些方面是具有启示性的。你当时有点，来吧，这就是《Get Back》。

sentences.en: And then you realize, oh, no, he doesn't even know that yet.
sentences.zh: 然后你意识到，哦，不，他甚至还不知道那个。

sentences.en: It's kind of an amazing sequence.
sentences.zh: 那是一个相当神奇的过程。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: But presumably that is what, that's what you first bonded with John Lennon over, that you both knew these chords, you knew this music.
sentences.zh: 但大概这就是你们最初和约翰·列侬建立联系的原因，你们都懂这些和弦，都懂这些音乐。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And that's what happened when you, well, did you first, what was the Walton Fate?
sentences.zh: 这就是当你……好吧，你第一次是什么时候，那个沃尔顿集市？

sentences.en: Was that the first time you met him or did you met him before?
sentences.zh: 那是你第一次见到他，还是之前就见过？

sentences.en: The first time I met John was at the Walton Fate.
sentences.zh: 我第一次见到约翰是在沃尔顿集市。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Through a friend of mine, my best friend at school was called Ivan Vaughn.
sentences.zh: 通过我的一个朋友，我在学校最好的朋友叫伊万·沃恩。

sentences.en: He was born on the 18th of June, 1942, same day as me in Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 他出生于1942年6月18日，和我同一天，在利物浦。

sentences.en: Um, and he knew John.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他认识约翰。

sentences.en: So he introduced me to John, but, uh, John pretty much knew what I knew.
sentences.zh: 所以他把我介绍给了约翰，但是，嗯，约翰基本上懂的我也懂。

sentences.en: Actually, in the very beginning, John was playing banjo chords on his guitar because his mum had taught him those chords.
sentences.zh: 其实刚开始时，约翰在吉他上弹的是班卓琴和弦，因为他妈妈教过他那些和弦。

sentences.en: So I would sort of say, well, you know, that could go like this and show him how we, how it was done on the guitar.
sentences.zh: 所以我就会说，嗯，你知道，那个可以这样弹，然后教他吉他是怎么弹的。

sentences.en: But it was all very just one on one.
sentences.zh: 但那一切都非常一对一。

sentences.en: And did you find that as the Quarrymen formed and then, you know, you became the beat, Silver Beatles and the Beatles and so on,
sentences.zh: 那么你是否发现，随着采石工人乐队的组建，然后，你知道，你们变成了银色披头士和披头士等等，

sentences.en: that as you became better and better and you're, you're kind of musically, you became more sophisticated, more knowing.
sentences.zh: 随着你们变得越来越好，你们在音乐上变得更加老练、更加内行。

sentences.en: Was the kind of infrastructure that enabled you to access music and also for your music to be promoted, kind of growing up around you, were there more record shops?
sentences.zh: 那种让你接触音乐以及推广你音乐的基础设施是否也在你周围成长？有更多的唱片店吗？

sentences.en: Were there, was it easier to get radio stations or whatever?
sentences.zh: 有吗？更容易找到电台之类的了吗？

sentences.en: So were you kind of, as the Beatles, moving towards a point where you could have a global market
sentences.zh: 所以作为披头士，你们是否正朝着一个可以拥有全球市场的方向发展，

sentences.en: in a way that maybe even Little Richard or maybe even Elvis hadn't back in kind of 1955 or something?
sentences.zh: 以一种甚至连小理查德或猫王在1955年左右可能都没有的方式？

sentences.en: We were hoping for that, you know, that was the, that was the idea that was prevalent at the time was that you would do what all these other people had done.
sentences.zh: 我们当时确实在期待那个，你知道，那是当时流行的想法，就是你要做所有其他人做过的事情。

sentences.en: Didn't quite know how you were going to do it, but I think that's half the battle is just having that bold ambition.
sentences.zh: 虽然不知道该怎么做，但我认为拥有那种大胆的野心就已经成功了一半。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So we just assumed we could do it if they've done it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只是假设，如果他们能做到，我们也能做到。

sentences.en: And we'd learned a lot of their tricks.
sentences.zh: 我们学到了他们很多技巧。

sentences.en: So when we showed each other how to do it and then came down to London and there were certain guys down here, mainly guys, that would know the stuff we knew.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们互相展示怎么做，然后来到伦敦时，这里有一些人，主要是男的，他们懂我们懂的东西。

sentences.en: So I remember the Isley Brothers was something that we knew, it was an act we knew because they did Twist and Shout, which we covered.
sentences.zh: 所以我记得艾斯利兄弟是我们知道的一个组合，因为他们唱了《Twist and Shout》，我们翻唱过。

sentences.en: And then you'd come down to London and someone would say, oh, you know the Isleys?
sentences.zh: 然后你来到伦敦，有人会说，哦，你认识艾斯利兄弟？

sentences.en: So there was that kind of in-crowd thing, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以当时有一种圈内人的感觉，你知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was a lot of fun.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那真的很有趣。

sentences.en: But kind of so, again, just to reiterate, it's so mad that this music was so kind of exclusive because you had to know.
sentences.zh: 但再次重申，这种音乐如此排外真是太疯狂了，因为你必须得知道。

sentences.en: If you knew, you knew.
sentences.zh: 如果你知道，你就知道。

sentences.en: And if you didn't, you didn't.
sentences.zh: 如果你不知道，你就是不知道。

sentences.en: Whereas now you can just kind of absorb it almost like osmosis.
sentences.zh: 而现在你可以像渗透一样吸收它。

sentences.en: No, it's nothing like it is now.
sentences.zh: 不，和现在完全不一样。

sentences.en: You can just hit a button and you can get all the music in the world.
sentences.zh: 你只要按个按钮，就能得到世界上所有的音乐。

sentences.en: Now then it was, I think it made it more special.
sentences.zh: 当时我觉得这让它变得更特别。

sentences.en: You know, if somebody had an interesting record.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果有人有一张有趣的唱片。

sentences.en: John's stepfather was a guy called Daikins, had some cool records.
sentences.zh: 约翰的继父是个叫戴金斯的人，有一些很酷的唱片。

sentences.en: So we'd go around to the house and play the records.
sentences.zh: 所以我们会去他家听那些唱片。

sentences.en: And there'd be things like Carl Perkins.
sentences.zh: 里面会有像卡尔·珀金斯这样的东西。

sentences.en: So that all got into our act.
sentences.zh: 所以这些都进入了我们的表演中。

sentences.en: So we'd learn it, get all the words down.
sentences.zh: 我们会学它，记下所有的歌词。

sentences.en: And so that was how you learned.
sentences.zh: 这就是你学习的方式。

sentences.en: It was just if someone had a record, you played the record and copied all the words out, worked out the chords and the riffs.
sentences.zh: 如果有人有唱片，你就放唱片，抄下所有的歌词，研究出和弦和即兴重复段。

sentences.en: It was a magic moment.
sentences.zh: 那是一个神奇的时刻。

sentences.en: I mean, I learned the riff to That Will Be The Day, Buddy Holly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我学会了巴迪·霍利的《That Will Be The Day》的即兴重复段。

sentences.en: I think Little Richard and Buddy Holly were your great favorites.
sentences.zh: 我想小理查德和巴迪·霍利是你最喜欢的歌手。

sentences.en: They were part of them.
sentences.zh: 他们是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Buddy Holly was great because he played guitar and he sang and he was out front, which not many of the singers did.
sentences.zh: 巴迪·霍利很棒，因为他弹吉他、唱歌，而且站在最前面，这在当时的歌手中并不多见。

sentences.en: Elvis had Scotty Moore, who played guitar for him.
sentences.zh: 猫王有斯科蒂·摩尔为他弹吉他。

sentences.en: But Buddy played the lead and did the riffs.
sentences.zh: 但巴迪自己弹主音，做即兴重复段。

sentences.en: So you'd learn off him.
sentences.zh: 所以你会向他学习。

sentences.en: And he wore glasses, which I always loved.
sentences.zh: 而且他戴眼镜，我一直很喜欢这一点。

sentences.en: And he wore glasses, which suddenly made life okay for John.
sentences.zh: 他戴着眼镜，这让约翰的生活突然变得好过了一些。

sentences.en: John was embarrassed.
sentences.zh: 约翰当时很尴尬。

sentences.en: Anytime he saw girls, he took the glasses off, you know.
sentences.zh: 每次见到女孩，他都会摘下眼镜，你知道。

sentences.en: So you're learning these songs, but then you start to write your own songs.
sentences.zh: 所以你在学习这些歌，但后来你开始写自己的歌了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I saw you interviewed on a film that came out recently, I think on the BBC, about your lost base.
sentences.zh: 我看到你最近在BBC播出的一部关于你丢失的贝斯的电影中接受采访。

sentences.en: And you were talking about how when you have a guitar, you would kind of take it away and sit in a private room and kind of nurse it.
sentences.zh: 你谈到当你有一把吉他时，你会把它带走，坐在一个私人的房间里，像呵护它一样。

sentences.en: Almost like going to a psychiatriSt.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像去看心理医生一样。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you would talk to the guitar and the guitar would talk back to you and it would talk to you in the form of a song.
sentences.zh: 你会和吉他说话，吉他也会回应你，它会以歌曲的形式和你交流。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I don't think that's what it's like for most people, but clearly that's what it's like for you.
sentences.zh: 我不认为大多数人是这样的，但显然你就是这样。

sentences.en: When did you discover that guitars could speak to you and give you songs?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候发现吉他可以和你交流并给你灵感的？

sentences.en: It must have been amazing to realise it.
sentences.zh: 意识到这一点一定很神奇。

sentences.en: I mean, I wrote my first song when I was 14.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我14岁时写了第一首歌。

sentences.en: And I suppose that's when I discovered it, you know.
sentences.zh: 我想我就是在那时发现它的，你知道的。

sentences.en: I remember the things that appealed to me about that song.
sentences.zh: 我记得那首歌里吸引我的地方。

sentences.en: The song was called I Lost My Little Girl.
sentences.zh: 那首歌叫《我失去了我的小女孩》（I Lost My Little Girl）。

sentences.en: And someone pointed out to me, my mum had died not too long before that.
sentences.zh: 有人向我指出，我母亲在那之前不久刚去世。

sentences.en: So probably at the back of my mind, a therapist would probably say, that's what this was about.
sentences.zh: 所以心理医生可能会说，这大概就是我潜意识里写这首歌的原因。

sentences.en: But the guitar was your therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 但吉他就是你的心理医生。

sentences.en: And the guitar was the therapist, really.
sentences.zh: 没错，吉他确实就是心理医生。

sentences.en: So, you know, I had a couple of musical ideas.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我当时有一些音乐上的想法。

sentences.en: The chords went down, went from G to G7 to C.
sentences.zh: 和弦走向是从G到G7再到C。

sentences.en: So there was a bam, bam, bam, bam.
sentences.zh: 所以节奏是砰、砰、砰、砰。

sentences.en: And then my melody went bam, bam, bam, bam against it.
sentences.zh: 然后我的旋律也跟着砰、砰、砰、砰地响。

sentences.en: So you had those little tricks that you just learned just from listening to music.
sentences.zh: 所以你会有一些从听音乐中学会的小技巧。

sentences.en: And, yeah, so you'd put them in and write a song.
sentences.zh: 是的，你会把它们用上，写出一首歌。

sentences.en: So once you'd written that first song, it was quite exciting and uplifting.
sentences.zh: 所以一旦你写出了第一首歌，那感觉相当令人兴奋和振奋。

sentences.en: So when did you and John start to realise that actually your songs were really good, that they could measure up to the songs that you'd been kind of learning and absorbing?
sentences.zh: 那么，你和约翰是什么时候开始意识到你们的歌真的很棒，能够与你们一直在学习和吸收的那些歌曲相媲美的呢？

sentences.en: I think we always thought they were good because we were cocky little bastards.
sentences.zh: 我想我们一直都觉得它们很棒，因为我们是自负的小混蛋。

sentences.en: But as they developed and we started to get a bit more mature in the writing,
sentences.zh: 但随着它们的发展，我们在创作上也开始变得成熟了一些，

sentences.en: I think then we started.
sentences.zh: 我想那时我们才开始（有这种感觉）。

sentences.en: I remember writing a song.
sentences.zh: 我记得写过一首歌。

sentences.en: We wrote a song together called From Me To You.
sentences.zh: 我们一起写了一首歌叫《From Me To You》。

sentences.en: And it was pretty straightforward, but in the middle of it, it went to a chord we'd never used before.
sentences.zh: 它非常直白，但在中间部分，它转到了一个我们从未用过的和弦。

sentences.en: And I remember thinking, wow, we're getting sophisticated.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时想，哇，我们变得老练了。

sentences.en: This is, we're in C to A minor.
sentences.zh: 我们从C转到了A小调。

sentences.en: Now suddenly we're doing a G minor.
sentences.zh: 现在突然又用了G小调。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So around about that period, you know, we started to think pretty good.
sentences.zh: 所以在那段时期，你知道，我们开始觉得我们相当不错。

sentences.en: And then you'd write a song, let's say like,
sentences.zh: 然后你会写一首歌，比如说，

sentences.en: I mean, what would always happen is one of us would come in with the idea and then the two of us would finish it up.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，通常的情况是，我们中的一个人带着想法过来，然后我们俩一起把它完成。

sentences.en: So something like Norwegian Wood, which was a John idea.
sentences.zh: 所以像《Norwegian Wood》这样的歌，就是约翰的想法。

sentences.en: And then we sat down and finished it together.
sentences.zh: 然后我们坐下来一起完成了它。

sentences.en: I think after that, we thought, oh, we're getting somewhere.
sentences.zh: 我想在那之后，我们想，哦，我们小有成就了。

sentences.en: Well, because that also, I mean, George introduced the sitar.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为那首歌也，我是说，乔治引入了西塔琴。

sentences.en: The sitar, yeah.
sentences.zh: 西塔琴，没错。

sentences.en: And it was a detail from John, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是约翰的一个细节，不是吗？

sentences.en: He didn't want to confess that he'd had a fling to Cynthia.
sentences.zh: 他不想向辛西娅承认他有过一段风流韵事。

sentences.en: That's what's said.
sentences.zh: 传闻是这么说的。

sentences.en: I don't know whether that's true or not.
sentences.zh: 我不知道这是不是真的。

sentences.en: I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我不确定。

sentences.en: But so around then, the songs are starting to move from I love you, you love me, she loves you, whatever, to more complicated, more almost novelistic stuff.
sentences.zh: 但就在那时，歌曲开始从“我爱你，你爱我，她爱你”之类的，转向更复杂、几乎像小说一样的内容。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I think that's when we started to think, wow, this is going somewhere, you know.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想那就是我们开始觉得“哇，这很有前途”的时候，你知道。

sentences.en: And then you would feel encouraged to write more than just the sort of I love you songs.
sentences.zh: 然后你会受到鼓励，去写更多不仅仅是“我爱你”之类的歌。

sentences.en: I just watched you talking through all the songs in the new album.
sentences.zh: 我刚才看你讲解新专辑里的所有歌曲。

sentences.en: And you said in that that your song Salesman's saying to me about your parents that you're kind of inspired by the example of Charles Dickens, looking back to his childhood.
sentences.zh: 你在里面提到你的歌《Salesman's》是关于你父母的，说你某种程度上受到了查尔斯·狄更斯回顾童年经历的启发。

sentences.en: And the sense I get with you and John as well is actually how kind of how literary you were as well, how informed by reading Lewis Carroll, Dickens or whatever.
sentences.zh: 我从你和约翰身上感受到的，实际上是你们在文学素养上有多深厚，以及受到刘易斯·卡罗尔、狄更斯等人作品的影响有多大。

sentences.en: So was that part of what was starting to feed into the songs around 1965?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是否也是1965年左右开始融入你们歌曲的一部分呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's one of the things that made the Beatles special was that three of us were grammar school boys.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为让披头士乐队与众不同的原因之一，就是我们中有三个人是文法学校的学生。

sentences.en: So we'd had to learn or be exposed to things like Lewis Carroll, as you say, Dickens.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不得不学习或接触像刘易斯·卡罗尔，正如你所说的，狄更斯这样的作品。

sentences.en: My case would be like Thomas Hardy and Shakespeare and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我个人的话，还会接触托马斯·哈代和莎士比亚之类的东西。

sentences.en: So even though we didn't like it at the time, because it was school, it was like, oh, this is boring, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以即使当时我们不喜欢，因为那是学校课程，觉得很无聊，你知道。

sentences.en: I think once we started writing, I started to realize, oh, it's finding its way in here somehow.
sentences.zh: 我想一旦我们开始创作，我就开始意识到，哦，它不知怎么地融入进来了。

sentences.en: It's keeping through.
sentences.zh: 它在渗透。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's just, you know, like sponges, we got it all in our being.
sentences.zh: 就像海绵一样，我们把这一切都吸收到了生命里。

sentences.en: And now when we're writing songs, you're starting to realize that like a rhyming couplet, which I would learn about through studying Hamlet from, you know, A-level or whatever.
sentences.zh: 现在当我们写歌时，你会开始意识到，比如押韵对句，这是我通过学习《哈姆雷特》学到的，你知道，在A-level考试或类似的时候。

sentences.en: And I always thought that was a cool idea of Shakespeare's.
sentences.zh: 我一直觉得那是莎士比亚的一个很酷的想法。

sentences.en: He just finished up the thing with, you know,
sentences.zh: 他只是用那个结束了整件事，你知道，

sentences.en: I'm going to do the bop and I'm going to do the bop.
sentences.zh: 我要做这个重音，我要做那个重音。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Goodbye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: That's the end of that.
sentences.zh: 那就是结局了。

sentences.en: So I was only years later, I realized I'd used that unwittingly.
sentences.zh: 所以多年后我才意识到，我无意中用了那个手法。

sentences.en: And in the end, the love you take is equal to the love you make.
sentences.zh: “最终，你付出的爱等于你得到的爱。”

sentences.en: Preceding that is Golden Slumbers, which you've kind of, it's literally word for word taken from an anthology of Elizabethan poetry.
sentences.zh: 在那之前是《Golden Slumbers》，你几乎是逐字逐句地从一本伊丽莎白时代的诗集中摘录出来的。

sentences.en: Again, something else that you said about the new album,
sentences.zh: 又是关于新专辑你提到的另一件事，

sentences.en: I listened to you talking, was you've got a song in it about a woman who has married a complicated man, but, you know, she's got the measure of him.
sentences.zh: 我听你谈论时，说里面有一首歌是关于一个嫁给了一个复杂男人的女人，但你知道，她看透了他。

sentences.en: And you were talking about how you love to write songs about people, almost like a kind of noveliSt.
sentences.zh: 你谈到你喜欢像小说家一样写关于人的歌。

sentences.en: Is Eleanor Rigby the first in that kind of sequence?
sentences.zh: 《Eleanor Rigby》是那个系列的第一首吗？

sentences.en: And it goes through Another Day and Jenny Wren.
sentences.zh: 然后接着是《Another Day》和《Jenny Wren》。

sentences.en: Yeah, probably.
sentences.zh: 是的，大概是吧。

sentences.en: No, I like that.
sentences.zh: 不，我喜欢那种感觉。

sentences.en: I like the filmic thing.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那种电影感。

sentences.en: You know, sometimes I'll write, and I love her, which is, you know,
sentences.zh: 你知道，有时我会写《And I Love Her》，那是，你知道，

sentences.en: I love some very straightforward and I think fine for what it is.
sentences.zh: 《And I Love Her》非常直白，我觉得作为一首歌它很好。

sentences.en: But then you'll, then I'll start to, you know, because you watch so many films, read so many books, that this character that I'd kind of known women like this,
sentences.zh: 但后来，我会开始，你知道，因为你看过那么多电影，读过那么多书，这个角色，我认识过这样的女人，

sentences.en: Eleanor Rigby, lonely old ladies on the housing estate where we lived, there were always a couple of old pensioners.
sentences.zh: 《Eleanor Rigby》，我们住的住宅区里孤独的老太太，总有那么几个退休老人。

sentences.en: And I would go around and offer to get their shopping for them and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我会过去主动提出帮她们买东西之类的。

sentences.en: And it was, it was very good because they'd start to tell me stories of the war.
sentences.zh: 这非常好，因为她们会开始给我讲战争时期的故事。

sentences.en: Well, I remember one of the old ladies showing me a crystal radio.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我记得其中一位老太太给我看了一台矿石收音机。

sentences.en: So it was great.
sentences.zh: 所以那太棒了。

sentences.en: It was very exciting.
sentences.zh: 非常令人兴奋。

sentences.en: So I liked these ladies.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢这些老太太。

sentences.en: So they were always a kind of special character for me.
sentences.zh: 所以她们对我来说一直是一种特殊的角色。

sentences.en: So I kind of wrote Eleanor Rigby from the perspective of one of those ladies.
sentences.zh: 所以我算是从其中一位老太太的角度写了《Eleanor Rigby》。

sentences.en: Yeah, because it's incredible kind of generosity and compassion in everything that you write.
sentences.zh: 是的，因为你写的一切中都有一种不可思议的慷慨和同情心。

sentences.en: And one other song that for me completely exemplified this was a beautiful song.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，另一首完全体现了这一点的歌是一首美丽的歌。

sentences.en: What's it called?
sentences.zh: 它叫什么名字？

sentences.en: Life Can Be Hard.
sentences.zh: 生活有时很艰难。

sentences.en: And people, when I say this song, Life Can Be Hard, you wrote it during COVID.
sentences.zh: 人们，当我提到这首歌《Life Can Be Hard》时，你是在新冠疫情期间写的。

sentences.en: People who haven't heard it may be expecting that it's going to be quite dark and somber.
sentences.zh: 没听过的人可能以为它会非常黑暗和忧郁。

sentences.en: I mean, it is so light and joyous.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它非常轻快和欢乐。

sentences.en: And that seemed to me the kind of, that is so Paul McCartney, that you can get joy out of something as awful as COVID.
sentences.zh: 这在我看来就是那种，非常保罗·麦卡特尼的风格，你能在像新冠疫情这样糟糕的事情中找到快乐。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, I think, you know, I think the people who are locked down with their family,
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想，你知道，我认为那些和家人一起被封锁的人，

sentences.en: who are forced to be with their family, if you love your family, that could be quite nice.
sentences.zh: 那些被迫和家人待在一起的人，如果你爱你的家人，那可能相当不错。

sentences.en: You know, you're suddenly an enforced family time.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你突然有了强制的家庭时光。

sentences.en: And I had the song and the minute I heard myself writing, Life Can Be Hard,
sentences.zh: 我有这个想法，当我听到自己写出“生活可能很艰难”时，

sentences.en: something told me to just say, but then.
sentences.zh: 有什么东西告诉我，只要接着说“但是”。

sentences.en: And then that's when we start to get it together again or whatever.
sentences.zh: 然后那就是我们开始重新振作起来的时候，或者诸如此类。

sentences.en: I didn't want to go down the dark route.
sentences.zh: 我不想走黑暗路线。

sentences.en: I wanted to say, yeah, life can be hard, but come on, gang.
sentences.zh: 我想说，是的，生活可能很艰难，但来吧，伙计们。

sentences.en: We're going to get this together.
sentences.zh: 我们要一起克服它。

sentences.en: We're going to make it happen, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们要让它好起来，你知道。

sentences.en: So it's like the Salesman's Saint song, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像《Salesman's》那首歌，你知道。

sentences.en: You know, they had to carry on.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们必须坚持下去。

sentences.en: I think it's a theme in my stuff, in my writing, that even though stuff is hard,
sentences.zh: 我认为这是我作品中的一个主题，即使事情很艰难，

sentences.en: you are going to have to carry on or let it defeat you.
sentences.zh: 你也必须坚持下去，否则就会被它打败。

sentences.en: And I think that's very much from the wartime years that all of us grew up in.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很大程度上源于我们所有人成长的战争年代。

sentences.en: Carry that weight.
sentences.zh: “承担那份重担”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But, you know, as I say, I never heard any of the uncles talk about the war.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，正如我所说，我从未听过任何叔叔谈论战争。

sentences.en: They would always have a joke, some great joke that they would tell you.
sentences.zh: 他们总会讲个笑话，一些他们会讲给你的绝妙笑话。

sentences.en: And so you kind of learned that even though that had been a terrible period, and we'd seen the film of Hitler's bombers clouding the sky,
sentences.zh: 所以你学会了，即使那是一段可怕的时期，我们看过希特勒的轰炸机遮天蔽日的电影，

sentences.en: and you'd seen the Belson pictures of the prisoners coming out in their striped uniforms, which is why I can never believe people deny the HolocauSt.
sentences.zh: 看过贝尔森集中营里囚犯穿着条纹制服走出来的照片，这就是为什么我永远无法相信有人会否认大屠杀。

sentences.en: I mean, that is so insane.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But, you know, we'd seen all of that, and yet the people we knew, people we were living amongst, had gone on and were now so glad to be away from that
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，我们看过所有那些，然而我们认识的人，我们生活在其中的人们，已经走出来了，现在很高兴能远离那段过去，

sentences.en: that now they were making something of their lives.
sentences.zh: 现在他们正在创造自己的生活。

sentences.en: And I think that's why there was quite a rich period for us, our generation, that we could now do good stuff and say, hey, it may be bad, but we can work this out.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是为什么对我们这一代人来说，那是一个相当丰富的时期，我们现在可以做好的事情，说，嘿，情况可能很糟，但我们可以解决它。

sentences.en: We can work it out.
sentences.zh: “我们可以解决它”（We Can Work It Out）。

sentences.en: We can work it out.
sentences.zh: 我们可以解决它。

sentences.en: So, I mean, I can understand hearing you say that, why now, so many decades on from your earliest years, that you might want to go back and look at those early years
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我能理解听你这么说，为什么在距离你早年生活几十年后的今天，你可能想回头看看那些早年岁月，

sentences.en: and see what kind of mirror it holds up to what we're going through now.
sentences.zh: 看看它为我们现在所经历的一切映照出了什么。

sentences.en: Can I just end by asking about your memories and the tricks that memory can play?
sentences.zh: 我能最后问一下关于你的记忆以及记忆可能玩弄的把戏吗？

sentences.en: You had a brilliant story about going on a milk float with George Harrison when you were, I don't know, were you 16 or something?
sentences.zh: 你有一个精彩的故事，关于你和乔治·哈里森坐牛奶运送车，当时你，我不知道，你16岁还是多少？

sentences.en: Yeah, it would have been.
sentences.zh: 是的，应该是吧。

sentences.en: We were hitchhiking, yeah.
sentences.zh: 我们在搭便车，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, and you've got a great story about a kind of electrical accident that happened to George, but he then, he thought that it happened to you.
sentences.zh: 是的，你有一个关于乔治发生的某种电气事故的精彩故事，但他后来以为那是发生在你身上。

sentences.en: So, can you just tell people what happened there?
sentences.zh: 所以，你能告诉大家那里发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, well, we were hitchhiking down south, which is what one of the songs on the new album is about, and we got a lift from a milk float, which was electric.
sentences.zh: 是的，嗯，我们在往南搭便车，这也是新专辑里其中一首歌的主题，我们搭上了一辆牛奶运送车，它是电动的。

sentences.en: Those were the only vehicles we knew that were electric.
sentences.zh: 那是我们当时唯一知道的电动交通工具。

sentences.en: It went about four miles an hour, but it was a lift, so we were quite happy.
sentences.zh: 它时速大约四英里，但能搭上一程，所以我们很高兴。

sentences.en: The driver was sitting on the right-hand side, then there was a battery in the middle, and then there was the passenger seat on the left-hand side,
sentences.zh: 司机坐在右边，中间有一个电池，左边是乘客座位，

sentences.en: and George sat on the battery, George Harrison sat on the battery,
sentences.zh: 乔治坐在电池上，乔治·哈里森坐在电池上，

sentences.en: and everything's going fine.
sentences.zh: 一切都很顺利。

sentences.en: We're going along, we're getting our lift, and then suddenly, bang, ah!
sentences.zh: 我们正走着，搭着便车，然后突然，砰，啊！

sentences.en: And he jumps up, like, what's that, what's wrong?
sentences.zh: 他跳了起来，就像，那是什么，怎么了？

sentences.en: And he had a pair of jeans with a zip on the pocket, and it had connected with the two points.
sentences.zh: 他穿了一条口袋上有拉链的牛仔裤，拉链连接到了那两个点上。

sentences.en: I thought, not on the crotch.
sentences.zh: 我以为，不是在胯部吧。

sentences.en: No, it wasn't the crotch.
sentences.zh: 不，不是胯部。

sentences.en: No, this was his back pocket.
sentences.zh: 不，这是他的后口袋。

sentences.en: So, he jumps up, and it had connected up, and the battery had given him a bolt.
sentences.zh: 所以，他跳了起来，它连接上了，电池给了他一下电击。

sentences.en: And later, when we got to our B&B, he showed me, yeah, he had a great big zip tattooed into his bum.
sentences.zh: 后来，当我们到达民宿时，他给我看了，是的，他的屁股上有一个大大的拉链纹身。

sentences.en: But?
sentences.zh: 但是？

sentences.en: But, and the point of what you were saying was, so that was always my story, and I told it to people.
sentences.zh: 但是，你刚才说的重点是，那一直是我讲的故事，我告诉过别人。

sentences.en: Then I met Olivia Harrison, George's widow, quite recently, and she was saying, oh, I love that story of you and George going down to Wales and you sitting on the battery
sentences.zh: 后来我最近见到了乔治的遗孀奥利维亚·哈里森，她说，哦，我喜欢那个你和乔治去威尔士，你坐在电池上，

sentences.en: and it connecting, and you've got a scar on your bum.
sentences.zh: 它连接上了，你屁股上留下了疤痕的故事。

sentences.en: I said, no, it wasn't me.
sentences.zh: 我说，不，那不是我。

sentences.en: It was George.
sentences.zh: 是乔治。

sentences.en: But I think it's amazing the way memory does that.
sentences.zh: 但我认为记忆以这种方式运作真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: It can just morph.
sentences.zh: 它会发生变形。

sentences.en: And it must be even harder for you because you've been so written about.
sentences.zh: 而且对你来说一定更难，因为关于你的报道太多了。

sentences.en: People know things about you that maybe never happened because it's been reproduced in countless books.
sentences.zh: 人们对你的了解可能从未发生过，因为这些事在无数书中被反复转载。

sentences.en: That's very true, and that is history.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，这就是历史。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: That is, and I now appreciate, through all the sort of wrong stories about the Beatles, I realise, you know, that Harold with the arrow in the eye,
sentences.zh: 确实是这样，我现在明白了，通过所有关于披头士乐队的那些错误故事，我意识到，你知道，哈罗德眼中插着箭的那件事，

sentences.en: oh, I get it, it was for the tapestry, or whatever, you know, all these little things.
sentences.zh: 哦，我明白了，那是为了挂毯，或者别的什么，你知道，所有这些小细节。

sentences.en: How can you have accurate history?
sentences.zh: 你如何才能获得准确的历史呢？

sentences.en: This is the perfect moat on which to end.
sentences.zh: 这是一个完美的护城河，以此作为结尾再好不过了。

sentences.en: Paul McCartney, thank you so much, and thank you, everyone, for listening.
sentences.zh: 保罗·麦卡特尼，非常感谢你，也感谢大家的收听。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I think of all the things that the rest of history has brought me,
sentences.zh: 我想，在《历史的余韵》带给我的所有收获中，

sentences.en: the chance to interview Paul McCartney is absolutely up there at the summit.
sentences.zh: 能有机会采访保罗·麦卡特尼绝对是巅峰体验。

sentences.en: I mean, that's something that I've dreamed of doing since I was about eight,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是我从八岁左右就开始梦想的事情，

sentences.en: and it was an amazing experience to have him come down the steps from the production booth in which George Martin had messaged them when they recorded,
sentences.zh: 当他从乔治·马丁当年给他们录制唱片时传话的制作室走下台阶时，那真是一次奇妙的经历，

sentences.en: please, please, me, gentlemen, you've just recorded your first number one, and there was Paul McCartney coming down the steps, having a little chat with him.
sentences.zh: “请，请，我，先生们，你们刚刚录制了你们的第一首冠军单曲”，保罗·麦卡特尼就这样走下台阶，和我聊了几句。

sentences.en: It was just amazing.
sentences.zh: 真是太神奇了。

sentences.en: When I began the interview, there was a kind of slight tightening of the vocal cords, I think, but he was amazingly generous,
sentences.zh: 采访刚开始时，我的声带有点紧绷，我想，但他非常慷慨，

sentences.en: amazingly personable.
sentences.zh: 非常有亲和力。

sentences.en: I know he's done a million interviews, so he's very skilled at putting interviewers, getting them to kind of feel easy, but it really did feel like a conversation.
sentences.zh: 我知道他接受过一百万次采访，所以他非常擅长让采访者放松，让他们感到自在，但这确实感觉像是一场真正的对话。

sentences.en: The only time when it didn't was when Paul started talking about the recording of Norwegian Wood, and I abstracted myself,
sentences.zh: 唯一一次感觉不像对话的时候，是保罗开始谈论《挪威的森林》的录制过程，我当时走神了，

sentences.en: I suddenly looked down and thought, here I am in Abbey Road, listening to Paul McCartney talk about how John Lennon wrote Norwegian Wood,
sentences.zh: 我突然低头想，我竟然身处艾比路录音室，听着保罗·麦卡特尼讲述约翰·列侬是如何写出《挪威的森林》的，

sentences.en: and my mind went completely blank at that point, and I had this great lurch of panic, thinking, what on earth am I going to talk to him about now?
sentences.zh: 那一刻我的大脑完全一片空白，我感到一阵巨大的恐慌，心想，接下来我到底该和他聊什么呢？

sentences.en: But actually, the interview flowed in all kinds of ways that I wasn't entirely expecting, which is kind of what made it so fun, and I thought, especially at the end
sentences.zh: 但实际上，采访以各种我完全没预料到的方式展开了，这正是它如此有趣的原因，我想，特别是在最后，

sentences.en: when he started talking about the unknowability of the past, and is the Bay of Tapestry adequate evidence for the Battle of Hastings?
sentences.zh: 当他开始谈论过去的不可知性，以及贝叶挂毯是否足以作为黑斯廷斯战役的证据时，

sentences.en: And I kind of felt then that maybe that was a comparison that he'd never previously drawn in any previous interview.
sentences.zh: 我当时觉得，这可能是一个他以前在任何采访中从未提出过的比较。

sentences.en: I may be wrong on that, but if so, then I feel very proud, wonderful that of all the things that he could have first talked about his take on the Battle of Hastings,
sentences.zh: 我可能错了，但如果是这样，我会感到非常自豪，太棒了，在他所有可以谈论的话题中，他第一次谈论他对黑斯廷斯战役的看法，

sentences.en: it was The Rest is History.
sentences.zh: 竟然是在《历史的余韵》节目里。
